newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission denies foot and mouth report.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission denies foot and mouth report.

text.p: The European Commission has no secret report on the danger of a European Union foot and mouth epidemic, an official said on Wednesday.
Jose Happart, a member of the European Parliament's committee of inquiry into BSE, told Belgian radio that foot and mouth was to be the subject of an explosive report "that is being kept secret".
He said vaccination against the disease ended in the EU in 1990 for "budgetary reasons".

"There is no such report. A report on management aspects of the veterinary unit was given to the BSE inquiry but there is no fear of any epidemic and nor is the disease a danger to humans," the Commission official said.
Vaccination of animals was ended in 1991 since when there had been only three contained outbreaks of foot and mouth, all involving imported animals, he added.
Vaccination was ended because some member states had not adopted the policy and to apply it across the EU would have cost 900 million Ecus.
The cost of eradicating the three outbreaks since 1991 was put at 15 million Ecus and a vaccination programme offered no guarantee against the disease, the official said.
One reason for not continuing with vaccination was that it set up anti-bodies in tests by third country importers who could not then tell if an animal was infected.
"Vaccination would seriously damage the European Union's beef exports. As such, since there is no danger of the disease being harmful to humans, it is unnecessary," the official said.
The Commission is currently talking to neighbouring central and eastern European countries about eradicating the disease on their territories.
